newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn tax talks could drag throughout summer.
newsitem.headline: Bonn tax talks could drag throughout summer.

text.p: Sources in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) said on Friday talks to reach an agreement on a tax reform between the ruling coalition and opposition parties could drag through the summer break.
The German parliament's mediation committee set up working groups on Thursday to seek a compromise on a package of income tax cuts and agreed to meet again this month.
Participants said Kohl's coalition of CDU/CSU and Free Democrats (FDP) would meet opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens for tax talks on July 28 and 29.
The CDU/CSU sources said the committee would probably hand a compromise back to the Bundestag lower house of parliament for approval at the end of July or beginning of August in a special session.
If it rejects these, then the tax proposals in their original form would be returned to the Bundesrat upper house of parliament around the middle of August to be considered in a special session.

The SPD majority in the upper house, where Germany's 16 regional states are represented, could however again vote to quash the government's proposed reform, sending it back to the parliamentary committee for a possible second round of mediation.
If the lower house rejects the second compromise proposal, the bill is dead.
